questions.q: Why do native tools like Oracle's Data Pump or PostgreSQL's pg_dump alone not solve a full cross-platform migration?
options: They move data in and out of their own platform in a portable form, but none of them natively convert schema from one platform's format to another's
They are incapable of exporting any data at all
They only work on databases smaller than 1GB
They require a paid license unavailable to most DBAs
questions.explain: Native export/import tools are excellent for getting data out of the source platform, but schema conversion between platforms is a separate step.

questions.q: What is the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) commonly paired with, and why?
options: AWS Database Migration Service (DMS), because DMS handles data movement while SCT handles the schema and code translation DMS doesn't
Oracle Data Pump, because SCT can only convert Oracle-native export files
MySQL's mysqldump, because SCT is a MySQL-only tool
It works entirely standalone and is never paired with another migration tool
questions.explain: DMS moves and replicates data; SCT converts procedures, functions, views, and schema — a gap native tools and DMS itself don't fill alone.

questions.q: What does this lesson note about SQL Server Migration Assistant (SSMA) that's easy to assume incorrectly?
options: It moves data INTO SQL Server from platforms like Oracle or MySQL, not out of SQL Server — migration tooling isn't always one direction
It only works for migrating away from SQL Server, never into it
It is identical in function to AWS DMS
It has been discontinued and no longer exists
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly flags checking which direction a migration tool actually supports before relying on it.

questions.q: Why does change data capture (CDC)-based replication matter for a large, actively-used production database migration?
options: It lets the source database keep running while changes replicate continuously, so cutover becomes a short final step instead of a long downtime window
It permanently prevents any downtime from ever being needed, even during cutover itself
It eliminates the need for an initial full data load entirely
It only works for databases under 1,000 rows
questions.explain: CDC allows an initial full load followed by ongoing replication, shrinking the final cutover to pausing writes, draining remaining changes, and switching over.

The course ends here with no further chapters
